title: Coupling Static and Dynamic MPI Correctness Tools to Optimize Accuracy and Overhead
problem: Static MPI correctness tools produce false positives (lack runtime context); dynamic tools produce false negatives (limited coverage) and have high overhead. Combining them could improve accuracy while reducing overhead.
motivation: MPI programs are notoriously difficult to debug. Different tool classes have complementary strengths and weaknesses. A combined approach could leverage strengths of both: static tool's exhaustive analysis + dynamic tool's precise runtime information.
method: Coupled workflow forwarding static tool reports to dynamic tools; generic exchange format enabling interoperability; integration of CoVer (static), SPMD IR (static), and MUST (dynamic) for detecting MPI local data races; selective instrumentation of dynamic tool based on static hints
key_novelty: First coupled static-dynamic MPI tool workflow, with generic exchange format enabling interoperability and achieving synergistic accuracy/performance improvements
contributions: Coupled workflow design combining static and dynamic MPI correctness tools
Generic exchange format for static-to-dynamic tool communication
Integration of CoVer, SPMD IR, and MUST for data race detection
Elimination of static tool false positives through dynamic validation
Detection of previously missed races in dynamic tool (extending coverage)
Runtime overhead reduction up to 10x through selective instrumentation
Proof of concept for tool interoperability

metrics.false_positive_reduction: Elimination of static tool false positives
metrics.coverage_improvement: Detection of races missed by dynamic tool alone

limitations: Focused on single bug class (local data races); generalization to other MPI errors unclear; exchange format specifics not detailed in abstract; scalability not addressed
